extracted.intended_audience: federally insured credit unions (FICUs), mortgage servicers, attorneys/escrow agents, third-party recordkeepers, and NCUA/regulatory compliance staff
extracted.subtask_description: Final rule and preamble amending 12 CFR part 745 governing share insurance coverage, recordkeeping, and treatment of trust accounts and mortgage servicing accounts for federally insured credit unions. It explains how insurance is calculated, what records may be relied on, and conditions for pass-through coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mortgage servicing accounts (MSA) coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Accounts maintained by a mortgage servicer, in a custodial or other fiduciary capacity, which are comprised of payments of principal and interest, shall be insured for the cumulative balance paid into the account by mortgagors, or in order to satisfy mortgagors' principal or interest obligations to the lender, up to the limit of the SMSIA per mortgagor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to MSAs held in custodial/fiduciary capacities; cumulative balances attributable to each mortgagor are insured up to the standard maximum share insurance amount (SMSIA) per mortgagor. The Board adopted this text as §745.3(a)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of tax and insurance premium payments in MSAs
rubrics_metrics.description: Accounts maintained by a mortgage servicer comprised of payments by mortgagors of taxes and insurance premiums shall be added together and insured in accordance with paragraph (a)(2) of this section for the ownership interest of each mortgagor in such accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tax/insurance-premium collections in MSAs are aggregated and insured under the general rules for ownership interests (paragraph (a)(2)), rather than treated under the principal/interest MSA rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record sources for establishing interests in accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: If the account records of an insured credit union disclose the existence of a relationship which may provide a basis for additional insurance, the details of the relationship and the interest of other parties in the account must be ascertainable either from the records of the credit union or the records of the member, maintained in good faith and in the regular course of business by the member or by some person or entity that has undertaken to maintain such records for the member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly allows the NCUA to look to records maintained by agents, custodians, fiduciaries, or third parties when those records are kept in good faith and in the regular course of business. This clarifies previous uncertainty about whether third-party records qualify as 'records of the member.'

rubrics_metrics.name: NCUA discretion on record sufficiency and chain of records
rubrics_metrics.description: The NCUA retains discretion to determine when records are maintained on behalf of a member, in good faith and in the regular course of business; ultimately, the NCUA must be able to establish ownership interests by following the chain of records maintained by parties at each level of the relationship from the account records maintained at the FICU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when third-party records exist, the agency will exercise judgment about their sufficiency and must be able to trace ownership through multi-tiered fiduciary relationships. Provides for case-by-case determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elimination of trustee/settlor signature-card requirement for trust account records
rubrics_metrics.description: The former requirement that the account records of a FICU in connection with a trust account disclose the name of both the settlor (grantor) and the trustee and contain an account signature card executed by the trustee is removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NCUA concluded this requirement posed an unnecessary burden and removed it to reduce complexity and align with FDIC practice; the change is intended to simplify recordkeeping obligations for FICUs and members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint account co-owner interest presumption
rubrics_metrics.description: The interests of the co-owners of a joint account shall be deemed equal, unless otherwise stated on the insured credit union's records in the case of a tenancy in common.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is substantively retained (moved to a different paragraph). If the FICU's records indicate otherwise (e.g., tenancy in common), that record controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: IOLTA and similar escrow account pass-through coverage conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Pass-through coverage for IOLTAs and other similar escrow accounts will only be available if the recordkeeping requirements of §745.2(c)(1) and the relationship disclosure requirements of §745.2(c)(2) are satisfied; funds attributable to each client/principal will be insured on a pass-through basis in whatever right and capacity the client or principal owns the funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An IOLTA or similar escrow account must be titled as such and underlying account records of the insured credit union must sufficiently indicate the existence of the attorney/escrow-agent–client relationship. The details of the relationship must be ascertainable from FICU records or from records maintained in good faith and in the regular course of business by the attorney/escrow agent or a person/entity acting on their behalf. The NCUA will determine sufficiency in its sole discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: General trust-account coverage calculation (SMSIA × beneficiaries)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposited trust funds are insured in an amount up to the SMSIA multiplied by the total number of beneficiaries identified by each grantor, up to a maximum of five beneficiaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the common, simplified calculation the final rule applies to informal revocable trusts, formal revocable trusts, and irrevocable trusts; it replaces prior separate formulas and merges trust categories for simplicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation of trust funds by grantor
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposited trust funds that pass from the same grantor to beneficiaries are aggregated for the purposes of determining coverage under this section, regardless of whether those funds are held in connection with an informal revocable trust, formal revocable trust, or irrevocable trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All trust funds from the same grantor are counted together when applying the per-grantor beneficiary calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate insurance coverage for trust funds
rubrics_metrics.description: The share insurance coverage provided under this section is separate from coverage provided for other funds at the same federally insured credit union.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trust-account coverage does not reduce or merge with the member's other account coverage at the same FICU; it is a distinct category of coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of equal allocation among multiple grantors
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise specified in the account records of the federally insured credit union, deposited funds held in connection with a trust established by multiple grantors are presumed to have been owned or funded by the grantors in equal shares.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FICU account records may rebut the presumption if they show different ownership/allocation among grantors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible and ineligible trust beneficiaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Beneficiaries include natural persons and qualifying charitable organizations; beneficiaries do not include the grantor of a trust or a person/entity that only obtains an interest if one or more named beneficiaries are deceased. Future trusts named as beneficiaries are not treated as beneficiaries; beneficiaries are the natural persons or organizations who will receive the funds through those future trusts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies which classes of recipients count toward the per-grantor beneficiary tally; excludes contingent or derivative beneficiaries and the grantor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal revocable trust payable to a formal trust treated as formal trust
rubrics_metrics.description: If an informal revocable trust designates the account owner's formal trust as its beneficiary, the informal revocable trust account will be treated as if titled in the name of the formal trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures consistent treatment where an informal trust's beneficiary is a formal trust; the informal account inherits formal-trust treatment for coverage purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions from trust-account coverage (co-owner-as-sole-beneficiary; employee benefit plans)
rubrics_metrics.description: Revocable trust co-owners that are sole beneficiaries of a trust are treated as joint ownership funds under §745.8; deposited funds of employee benefit plans, even if held in connection with a trust, are treated as employee benefit plan funds under §745.9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies specific situations where trust-account rules do not apply and alternative account-treatment provisions govern coverage.
